paras: The mob pursuit of William Daniels took place in October 1903 near the Tug River between West Virginia and Kentucky, when friends of a bartender named Trimble Sparks formed a mob to deal out "summary justice" to the Black man accused of shooting him. According to a dispatch from Inez, Kentucky, the man escaped by a roundabout route and asked for protection at Williamson, West Virginia. A wire report named him as William Daniels and said an armed posse was pursuing him; no report of his capture or trial appears in the coverage.

Trimble Sparks was a bartender, whom the Inez dispatch described as eighteen years old and employed by a "Capt. Huddleson." A later obituary in the Big Sandy News of Louisa, Kentucky, called him Green Trimble Sparks, son of Silus Sparks, and gave his age as 21. Every account traced the shooting to a refused drink: whiskey in the Inez dispatch, a drink "on credit" in the Huntington wire, and liquor in the obituary.

The Inez dispatch, dated October 23, said Sparks had been shot through the head "last night" in his saloon "just above Warfield" by a Black man whose name had not been learned. A Huntington, West Virginia, dispatch of the same date instead placed the shooting "to-day," named the shooter as William Daniels, and reported that Sparks had been killed. According to the wire, Daniels escaped and was thought to have crossed the Tug River into Kentucky, and "an armed posse" was formed to pursue him.

The Inez dispatch described the pursuers as friends of Sparks who "formed a mob to dea[l] out summary justice to the negro." It added that the man, "it is said," escaped the mob by a circuitous route, reached Williamson, West Virginia, and there asked for protection from mob violence.

Sparks did not die at once, according to an obituary datelined Meta, Kentucky, November 10, and printed in the Big Sandy News on November 20. It said he had been shot on October 18 at Fairfax, West Virginia, "lingered until Nov. 9th," and had been engaged to marry Dixie Reynolds on December 25. The obituary did not mention the accused man or the mob, and no report of Daniels's arrest, an inquest or a trial appears in the coverage.

Distant papers carried the episode as a brief wire item from Huntington that reported the pursuit but no mob. The Indianapolis Journal ran it on October 24 under the headline "Armed Posse After a Negro" and called Daniels "the murderer," while the Washington Evening Star printed a one-sentence version on October 26 saying Sparks was "instantly killed." In Chicago, the Polish-language Dziennik Chicagoski gave the item a single sentence on October 24, calling Daniels a "murzyn" who had fled toward Kentucky.

Only the Big Sandy News, published near the scene, reported a mob and its aim of "summary justice," in the Inez dispatch it printed on October 30, split across two columns of its fourth page. That account recorded the man's escape and his appeal for protection without comment on the mob. All of the white reports identified the accused by race as "a negro"; no Black-press coverage of the episode was found.

The reports disagree on where the shooting happened: the Inez dispatch placed it in a saloon above Warfield, the wire at Huntington, and the obituary at Fairfax, West Virginia. They also differ on the date, given as October 18 in the obituary, the night of October 22 in the Inez dispatch and October 23 in the wire, and on whether Sparks died at once or three weeks later. The obituary, written locally after his death, gives the most specific account of the date and his death, while the wire's Huntington dateline may mark only where the dispatch was filed.
The wire's "armed posse" and the Inez dispatch's mob may describe the same pursuit, but only the Inez dispatch said the pursuers meant to deal out summary justice.

reader.title: Mob pursuit of William Daniels
bases: Friends of the shooting victim formed a mob to deal out summary justice to the Black man accused of the shooting and pursued him, but he escaped (A4, A5; posse pursuit in A1); a threatened lynching with no one killed by the mob.

The mob sought to deal out 'summary justice' over the shooting of Trimble Sparks (A4, A5), but the accused man escaped to Williamson and no report says anyone was killed (A5, A1); the pursuit was a threatened lynching, not a completed one.

The Huntington wire (A1) and the separate Inez dispatch (A4, A5) agree that a Black man shot the bartender Trimble Sparks over a refused drink and was pursued by an armed group, though only the Inez dispatch calls it a mob bent on summary justice and the two differ on place, date and Sparks's death.

accounts.label: Huntington wire
accounts.gist: Daniels shot and killed Sparks after being refused a drink on credit, escaped, probably across the Tug river into Kentucky, and an armed posse went in pursuit.

accounts.label: Inez, Ky., dispatch
accounts.gist: An unnamed Black man shot Sparks through the head in a saloon above Warfield; Sparks's friends formed a mob to deal out summary justice, but the man escaped to Williamson, W. Va., and asked protection.

accounts.label: Local obituary
accounts.gist: Sparks was shot at Fairfax, W. Va., on Oct. 18 by a Black man over a refused drink of liquor and died on Nov. 9.

framing.detail: The Indianapolis Journal headlined the wire 'Armed Posse After a Negro' and called Daniels 'the murderer'; the Evening Star and Dziennik Chicagoski ran one-sentence versions.
The Big Sandy News printed the Inez dispatch reporting the mob's aim of 'summary justice' and the man's appeal for protection without comment.

conflicts.note: The wire's Huntington may be only the filing point; it also says the accused crossed the Tug river into Kentucky. The local obituary is the most specific.
The obituary, written after the death by a local friend, gives an explicit date.

versions.value: Shot through the head; death not stated

conflicts.note: The later local obituary is better evidence of the date of death than the first-day wire.

West Virginia per the wire and obituary; the Inez, Ky., dispatch names no state for the saloon
William Daniels (named in the wire), Black, threatened, not harmed
Accused of shooting bartender Trimble Sparks after being refused a drink
threatened: a mob formed and pursued but never reached the man
Trimble Sparks died of the shooting attributed to the accused (race not stated); the mob killed no one
in pursuit; escaped to Williamson and asked protection
Friends of Sparks forming a mob; an armed posse
Three independent reports (Huntington wire, Inez dispatch, local obituary) plus two wire reprints, in four papers

info: Shooting on October 18 (obituary), the night of October 22 (Inez dispatch dated Oct. 23, 'last night'), or October 23 (Huntington wire, 'to-day'); pursuit followed immediately
Saloon 'just above Warfield' (Inez dispatch); Huntington, W. Va. (wire); Fairfax, W. Va. (obituary); the accused fled to Williamson, W. Va.
A Black man, named William Daniels in the Huntington wire and unnamed in the Inez dispatch; threatened, not harmed
Accused of shooting bartender Trimble Sparks, who had refused him a drink (on credit per the wire; of whiskey per the Inez dispatch)
'Friends' of Sparks who 'formed a mob' (Inez dispatch); 'an armed posse' (Huntington wire)
